messages.subject: Regarding RRO install
parts:
Hi,
#Issue1:
I am trying to build RRO from source on my RHEL6 machine.
I went through README & executed build.sh
i got :
./build.sh: line 21: xbuild: command not found
./build.sh: line 22: mono: command not found

i understand that these commands are not on my system & probably these are used for cross compiling/porting windows based code to linux. Main reason for building from source was that i wanted to select my compiler (intel) & the install location (to a custom/ non standard path).
  • So is there a way where i can install RRO on my RHEL to a different nonstandard/custom location (source build/binary installation) ?
-----------------------------------
#Issue2:
also i feel i am confused with the terms CRAN , MRAN , RRO and R.

CRAN seems to be a package repo server+ (official/original?) maintainer for R source (downloaded R from wget https://cran.rstudio.com/src/base/R-3/R-3.2.3.tar.gz)
MRAN seems to maintain a fork of R language as well as a package repo server

  • How is CRAN's R different from MRAN's RRO, in other words, can i install R's package on RRO and vice versa? (https://www.r-project.org/about.html  pointed me to CRAN server)
Any help/hint will be very useful (for both issues).

Thanks & Regards
Puneet Singh

messages.author: 9ca0345d553844f2
messages.subject: Re: Regarding RRO install
parts:
The RRO 3.2.2 rpm for RHEL6 should be relocatable.

CRAN is a collection of sites, carrying the same content (R distributions, extensions, documentation, packages, binaries).

MRAN is Microsoft's site where you can find information about R, download Revolution R Open, and look up R Packages. MRAN includes tools to explore R Packages and R Task Views, making it easy to find packages to extend R's capabilities. It also provides access to daily snapshots of the packages on CRAN to increase the reproducibility of your scripts. MRAN is updated daily.

RRO is an enhanced distribution of R. Enhancements include multi-core processing, a fixed CRAN repository date, and reproducible R with the checkpoint package. RRO 3.2.2 includes R 3.2.2,  and is therefore fully compatibility with all packages, scripts and applications that work with that version of R.

Cheers,
Josee Martens
